title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative:
The institutional capacity of employers' organizations in Tanzania is being strengthened to promote sustainability, decent work, and gender equality within the business sector. The Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE) is at the forefront of initiatives to enhance awareness and implementation of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices, combat gender-based violence (GBV), and foster inclusive development.
In response to increasing demand for ESG expertise, ATE is developing a tailored training program for member firms, including adapting international ESG materials for the Tanzanian context. This initiative supports businesses in aligning with regulatory requirements, improving sustainability practices, and gaining access to funding through partnerships with financial institutions. Concurrently, ATE continues its leadership in addressing workplace GBV by conducting training, awareness campaigns, and surveys, complementing national plans to end violence against women and children.
Through collaboration with international partners, including the International Training Centre of the International Labour Organization (ITCILO), ATE is advancing corporate responsibility and workplace safety. These efforts aim to position Tanzanian enterprises as regional leaders in ESG practices while promoting gender equality, labor rights, and decent work in alignment with global sustainable development goals.
Expected outcomes include increased adoption of ESG principles across member firms, improved workplace grievance mechanisms, enhanced gender-sensitive leadership, and strengthened resilience to climate-related risks. ATE's proactive approach ensures sustainable business practices while contributing to broader national and global development objectives.
